Consult Summary:
- Acute, new-onset left-sided headache with visual disturbances and nausea/vomiting suggestive of migraine with aura; patient requires home treatment with escalation to urgent neurological assessment if not improving.

History:
- Presenting complaint: One-sided (left) headache with blurred vision and zigzag visual phenomena, accompanied by dizziness and nausea/vomiting.
- Onset and progression: Began this morning with sudden onset; ongoing for several hours (about 4 hours since onset); pain described as about 6/10 at worst.
- Symptom characteristics: Unilateral left head pain; visual disturbances (zigzag lines, blurred vision); worsened by movement; cannot tolerate screens.
- Exposures and prior history: Had prior kidney stones; this is the first time with this type of headache. Family history notable for migraines (mother) and hypothyroidism (mother).
- Medications: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) taken ~3 hours ago without relief; no regular medications.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Pregnancy status: Not pregnant.
- Pertinent negatives: No focal weakness, no difficulty walking or slurred speech reported; no neck stiffness or fever mentioned.
- Patient concerns: Worries about serious causes (e.g., brain tumor or stroke) due to severity and new presentation.

Past Medical History:
- Kidney stones (history noted).
- No other chronic medical conditions documented.
- Family history: Mother with migraines; mother with hypothyroidism.

Medications:
- Paracetamol (acetaminophen): dose/route/frequency not documented; taken approximately 3 hours ago with no relief.
- Ibuprofen: recommended as part of migraine management; dose/route/frequency not documented (not yet taken).
Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Not documented beyond pregnancy status (not pregnant); other social factors not provided.

Family History:
- Migraines (mother) and hypothyroidism (mother).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- General: Not recorded.
- Head/Neck/HEENT: Not formally documented; patient reports visual symptoms.
- Neurological: No focal neurological deficits reported; patient able to walk; no weakness or gait disturbance described.
- Additional notes: Patient reported photophobia (discomfort with screens) and nausea; movements worsen symptoms.

Investigations:
- Not performed or not recorded in this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Working diagnosis: Migraine with aura presenting as new unilateral left-sided headache with visual disturbances, nausea/vomiting, and photophobia; no focal neurological deficits observed clinically to date.
- DDx Integration (top 3 aligned with the case):
  - Migraine with aura
    - Supporting: unilateral left-sided headache, visual aura (zigzag lines, blurred vision), nausea/vomiting, photophobia; triggered by movement; family history of migraines supports susceptibility.
    - Opposing: first-time presentation in adulthood; however migraines can present de novo.
  - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) / acute intracranial vascular catastrophe
    - Supporting: sudden onset this morning with vomiting and dizziness.
    - Opposing: no thunderclap headache, neck stiffness, or altered mental status; no focal deficits yet.
  - Ischemic stroke / TIA with visual symptoms
    - Supporting: abrupt onset with visual disturbance and dizziness.
    - Opposing: no motor/sensory deficits; patient is functioning otherwise; age and risk factors limited in data.
- Issue 1: Migraine with aura
  - Diagnosis/Status: Likely migraine with aura based on clinical presentation.
  - Plan:
    - Medications: Ibuprofen with antiemetic; dose/route/frequency not documented; advise oral intake and avoid triggers.
    - Nonpharmacologic: Hydration; sugary/carbonated drinks (e.g., Coca-Cola) as part of initial relief strategy; avoid screens.
    - Monitoring: If symptoms improve within 30–40 minutes, continue supportive care; if not improved or worsens, pursue migraine-specific therapies as movement up the treatment ladder and arrange a full neurological assessment today.
    - Follow-up: Attend scheduled assessment today; cancel appointment if symptoms resolve sooner.
- Issue 2: Rule out acute intracranial process (SAH/stroke) given sudden onset
  - Diagnosis/Status: Consider if red flags persist or worsen.
  - Plan:
    - Immediate neurological assessment today if symptoms persist or worsen.
    - Escalate to imaging or urgent in-person evaluation if red flags develop (e.g., new weakness, speech changes, altered mental status).
- Issue 3: Safety-netting and follow-up
  - Plan:
    - If symptoms respond to treatment and improve, the patient may cancel the visit.
    - Seek urgent care if headache worsens, new focal deficits develop, confusion, neck stiffness, fever, or persistent vomiting.
    - Education provided regarding migraine patterns and when to seek urgent care.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals not recorded; formal neurological exam details not documented beyond absence of focal deficits; no imaging or labs ordered or discussed.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None identified; DDx items aligned with the presentation; red-flag considerations acknowledged but not escalated beyond the planned neurology assessment.
- Transcript quality: Conversation covered key symptoms and history; occasional minor transcription gaps (e.g., exact timing/dose of paracetamol, exact vitals), but sufficient for structured note.

Document quality:
- Allergies: None documented.
- Med reconciliation: Not fully complete (no current chronic meds); paracetamol recent use recorded.
- Neuro exam: Not formalized beyond patient-reported absence of focal deficits.
- Imaging/lab data: Not obtained in this encounter.
